messages.subject: Re: [stan] test nan input for functions in src/stan/agrad/rev/functions/ (#845)
parts:
After opening up this can of worms, I'm not sure if the right thing to do is to enforce all of this inside the functions or expect the functions to be called with "good" values.

It makes sense, but might be too much of a performance hit. The cases I'm worried about are the few functions that take nan and output reasonable numbers like 1 or 0.

On Aug 12, 2014 4:44 PM, "Peter Li" <notifi...@github.com> wrote:

Ok and then for functions like fmax, fma, if_else, etc. when NaN is passed in, the gradients return 0 or 1. For instance,

    inline var fmax(const stan::agrad::var& a,
                    const stan::agrad::var& b) {
      return a.vi_->val_ > b.vi_->val_ ? a : b;
    }

is going to give gradient 1 for both NaN inputs so should we just throw in this case?

—

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] [stan] test nan input for functions in src/stan/agrad/rev/functions/ (#845)
parts:
Does it make sense to try to have

(1) the autodiff lib follow C++ functions in
throwing or not throwing?

(2) Stan follow C++ functions in throwing or not?

I tried to have both of these follow C++ as closely as
possible, though I'm no longer sure (2) is such a good idea.

I do think that whatever we decide for (2), we should be
consistent, which may mean wrapping C++ built-in and
standard library functions for double valued inputs, because
those don't throw as is.

- Bob
